text: Welcome to week seven of the official
NASCAR Gen 4 Cup Series. And this week,
you'll be taking on the newly repaved
Iowa Speedway for 100 laps.
Before you head out for qualifying, turn
a few laps in practice and get used to
the difference in grip between the
lighter and darker pavement. You'll
quickly notice that the darker, fresher
pavement offers you a smoother ride
through the corner. So, as you might
expect, you want to aim for that on both
ends of the track. As you may have also
noticed, the transition between the
different qualities of pavement can get
sketchy quickly. So, as you get your
tires up to temperature, try keeping the
car down on the fresh pavement in the
corners. In my experience turning laps
here, the outside doesn't serve much
purpose at all throughout the session.
So, I would advise to keep the car in
the dark as you build momentum in turns
three and four to take the white flag.
Ease onto the throttle and fire the car
down the front stretch until you can see
the track drop off into turn one. Keep
your eyes on the white line, trail brake
gently, get the car down to the bottom,
and ease back onto the gas to keep the
weight planted on the right side. Lean
further on the throttle and keep the car
on the dark as you point yourself out of
the corner. Hit turn three with the same
idea. Truck the car low. Ease back onto
the throttle and ride the fresh pavement
to the exit. But this time, you want to
tread lightly as the transition out of
turn four can hit you hard if you aren't
careful. Give yourself a moment before
you get back to full power as you finish
your run. Let's see that lap again.

Once The race begins, you want to take
it easy in second gear. Some of you
might be taking the green right where
the pavement transitions, so short
shifting may be your key to survival.
The wheel spin on the lighter pavement
only gets worse throughout the race, so
be ready for that, as well as the wrecks
that may start around you as a result.
With the fresh pavement on the insides
of the corners, that's where you'll want
to be. But as the run goes on, you'll
find that is incredibly easy to
overdrive the bottom. I ran 25 laps with
times ranging from 23.7 to 24.3 seconds,
and my wear ended up leaning toward the
right front. It wasn't by much, but
after lap 15, it became evident that I
was pushing the nose too hard on the
exit of turn four.
As tempting as it may be to ride that
dark pavement all the way up the track,
you can overheat your tires quickly if
you're too reliant on it, and eventually
you'll find yourself getting closer to
the wall earlier than you'd like as you
exit the corners. To limit this effect,
try waiting longer through the center to
finish pivoting the car and exit
slightly lower to even out the stress on
your right side tires. You'll still be
tracking up to the wall and exit, but
try aiming slightly further ahead
relative to where the dark pavement ends
before you finish your corner.
With that handling in mind, not entirely
certain if the second lane will be
viable on offense over the course of the
long run. Assuming the grip stays the
same across the entire dark section,
you'll likely be better off staying as
low as you can through the center of the
corner. As you may have noticed, the
left side wear is once again almost
non-existent. After what would have been
a quarter of the race under green, I saw
only 2% of wear on both tires and ended
up with temperatures that were more than
manageable. Assuming the race continues
under green, you could bet that they
would still be above 90% by the
checkered flag. So, in the case that you
end up with a light race caution, I'd
say take the gamble and go for right
side tires only.
You'll only need a splash of fuel this
week. So, if the cautions pile up, you
could very well run this whole race on a
single tank. With how treacherous the
restarts will be this week, you may be
in for another good week of high pacing.
So, get familiar with the hot keys for
your ignition and starter as every drop
of fuel counts. If you can manage your
fuel, keep your right side tires happy,
and adapt to the fresh pavement, you
might find yourself in a position to win
as the race winds down. Good luck.
